history: The records came first (the same afternoon; the eval PROVENANCE this file replaces pinned results.json and refutations.json). The package snapshot here was one session behind the grader that graded those records — taskset.py and forgeries.py stale, policies.py and __main__.py absent — which frontier's PORT-TO-CERT-MACHINE.md (session 17) named. why: The pinned rollouts are the RE-GRADED record; a grader that is not the one that graded them is a claim about a different set. eval/regrade.py measures exactly that against the stored raws and must report 0 rows moved — instruments/wiring/battery.py runs it every build.
rule: Copied byte-for-byte and pinned by sha256; frontier-apps has no git, so the hash is the only pin. The source tree is read-only. Nothing here is a lift from sin-mfg. Model calls (eval/run_models.py) are never made by a battery; the record is what was run there.

v020.what: lattice-claims 0.2.0, built 2026-10-04 for a training comparison: the exact grader (default) against an answer key (grader='answer_key'), the binary verdict of the complete instance, under which an abstention never scores. Every reply is scored under both; dims and mix are parameters that ride in every row.
v020.why: The pre-registered comparison for the Prime Intellect application: does a binary answer key train guessing where the exact grader trains decided abstention? Prior art, cited on the README: Kalai et al. 2025 (arXiv 2509.04664, the incentive argument) and TruthRL 2025 (arXiv 2509.25760, binary vs ternary reward under GRPO on knowledge QA). What is added here: every abstention is decided, so abstaining on a complete task scores 0 too.
